item.title: Recap of the first week learning go
item.description:

item.title: My Ultralearning Project Go + Backend
item.description:
I know, I know…

I already have a post where I talked about a Go roadmap, but I fell into a rabbit hole of learning.

AND I FOUND THE ULTRALEARNING BOOK.

I really fell in love with the idea and decided to embark on this journey on my own. That also meant changing my “roadmap”, because it is more of a project now and about learning a bunch of practices & methods of an “Ultralearner”. So basically, how to be really intense in short amounts of time, and thus get really impressive results.

item.title: My Roadmap for learning Go
item.description: So I’ve tried out a bunch of different programming languages since my interest in programming sparked, and I couldn’t really tell which I liked the most. I really liked the simplicity of Python, but hated its syntax. I really liked the syntax of C/C++ and its low-level power, but hated the linking & CMake. I mean, I have tried Go and liked it very much, but just stopped with Go for no exact reason…

item.title: Posting workflow with hugo, github and Obsidian
item.description:
So I wanted to start a blog page…

As everyone does, I first searched on Google “post blog ultra fast github free”. I stumbled on Hugo and really loved the variety of themes one could install, etc.

The Setup itself was not quite hard:

  • Setting up 2 repos:
    • A repo where you would draft and demo your page
    • A .github.io repo where it would actually be deployed
  • Creating a new Hugo project in the draft repo and choosing a theme
  • Setting up a submodule pub that would refer to the github.io repo and deploying the final build with hugo -t theme -d pub

OK, we got the really basic Hugo-GitHub setup, now how do we make it more quirky with Obsidian?

Since Hugo and literally any other blog posting framework use .md, I decided to use my beloved tool Obsidian, which I’ve used for 1+ years for high school, uni, and personal learning.
